topology: 16 nodes x4 H100, NVSHMEM star over the NIC with P2P disabled: ranks 1-63 push a full slot to rank 0, rank 0 answers each with slot/8
golden: none — assertions only, the same two case 16 runs at 4 ranks
workload_note: `asym_patterns hub 4096 3` at 64 PEs with NVSHMEM_DISABLE_P2P=1, so intra-node peers use the NIC too and every one of the 126 edges is verbs traffic. Not a suite case — 16 nodes is not something to spend on every board run — but it carries case 16's two assertions verbatim, by symlink, because both are closed-form in params.ranks and therefore say the same thing at 4 ranks and at 64. app_buffer_bytes is npes*slot*4 = 1 MiB, the hub's receive buffer, which is 16x case 16's and the point of the run: one object written by 63 distinct peers into 63 disjoint bands.

expect_fail_asserts.entity_close_accounted: hcoll leaks two memory regions per node leader, and it is not ours to fix. Measured over four allocations (plans/PLAN-20260812-0250-hcoll-mcast-leaks-two-mrs): hmca_mcast_vmc.so registers regions of 40, 8388608 and 20971520 bytes and deregisters only the 20971520 one, so exactly 2 ib_mem_region per rank with rank % 4 == 0 are opened and never closed — 32 of them here. It is a leak and not a missing door: every ibv_dereg_mr that library makes is visible in the caller trace, including the balanced one, and a free after finalize would still have printed a line. hcoll's multicast enables itself by node count, clean at 4 nodes and leaking at 8, so no suite case reaches it and this marker is one case wide. sql_check reports XPASS if HPC-X ever fixes it, which is the signal to delete this.
